content: Lubiprostone is indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) in adults at a dosage of 24 mcg taken orally twice daily. It is also indicated for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in women aged 18 years and older at a dosage of 8 mcg taken orally twice daily. Additionally, it is used for the treatment of opioid-induced constipation (OIC) in adults with chronic non-cancer pain, including those with chronic pain related to prior cancer or its treatment, who do not require frequent opioid dosage escalation (e.g., weekly), at a dosage of 24 mcg taken orally twice daily. The effectiveness of lubiprostone in patients taking diphenylheptane opioids, such as methadone, has not been established. Its safety and efficacy have not been fully determined in certain populations. Common adverse effects include nausea (8-29%), diarrhea (7-12%), headache (2-11%), abdominal pain (4-8%), abdominal distension (3-6%), flatulence (4-6%), vomiting (3%), loose stools (3%), edema (1-3%), abdominal discomfort (1-3%), dizziness (3%), chest discomfort or pain (2%), dyspnea (2%), dyspepsia (2%), fatigue (2%), and dry mouth (1%). Cardiovascular adverse effects, such as syncope, hypotension, and tachycardia, have been reported. Gastrointestinal complications, including ischemic colitis, may occur. General side effects include asthenia. Hypersensitivity reactions, such as rash, swelling, throat tightness, and malaise, have been observed. Musculoskeletal side effects, such as muscle cramps or spasms, may also occur. Patients with symptoms suggestive of mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction should undergo thorough evaluation to confirm the absence of obstruction before initiating therapy. Acute dyspnea, described as chest tightness and difficulty breathing, may occur within 30-60 minutes after the first dose. Patients should be instructed to contact their healthcare provider if dyspnea occurs. Lubiprostone should be avoided in patients with severe diarrhea, and patients should be informed of the potential for diarrhea during treatment. Taking the medication with food may reduce the likelihood of nausea. Dose adjustments may be necessary. Syncope and hypotension have been reported, with some cases requiring hospitalization. These events most commonly occurred in patients taking 24 mcg twice daily and were sometimes observed within an hour after the first or subsequent doses. Patients should be made aware of the risk of syncope and hypotension during treatment, particularly if other adverse reactions, such as diarrhea or vomiting, occur, as these may increase the risk. Following oral administration, plasma concentrations of lubiprostone are below the level of quantification; however, one of its metabolites, M3, has measurable systemic concentrations. There is no available data to inform the risk of adverse developmental outcomes associated with the drug. Additionally, no data exists regarding its presence in human milk or its effects on milk production. Lubiprostone should be administered with food and water. Capsules should be swallowed whole and not broken apart or chewed. The need for continuous therapy should be periodically assessed. The medication should be stored at 25°C (77°F), with excursions permitted between 15-30°C (59-86°F). It should be protected from light and extreme temperatures. This information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
